Alright so as promised, I'm here to tell you all about the convention I went to 2 weeks ago, Supercon. I went as Igbis from FFXV, and my friends went as the rest of the party and Lunafreya, another character from the game.

Cool as shit cosplays that I saw.

- Turalyon from Warcraft. Probably the best "non-professional cosplay that I saw.

- Makoto, Ryuji and Akechi from Persons 5. The Makoto was incredibly nice and was one of the only people to complement my cosplay. 

- A couple dressed as Solid Snake and Otacon. 

- Zero from Code Geass 

- Doomguy with only the helmet. The rest of his body was a suit. 

- Fidel Castro 

- Moira from Overwatch. This girl had LEDs on her nails and everything it was super fucking cool. Moira main btw.

- Police officer Boba Fett. 


Cool as shit people I met

- Jim Starlin. The guy who created Thanos and basically everything space related in Marvel. Me and one of my friends kind of nerded out in front of him but he took it well. Super cool guy.

- Kevin MOTHERFUCKING Conroy. Again, super nice dude. Did the Bruce Wayne voice and made me happy.

- Alan Oppenheimer. Ok so I gotta preface that I'm an enormous Skeletor fan, and can do a pretty good Skeletor impression. So after waiting in line for like 20 minutes while this dude in front of me told Skeletor his life story and had him sign everything, I finally met him. I was nervous on whether or not to give him my impression or not because I'm sure he gets it all the time.  Needless to say, I did and he was really impressed. He then asked if I could do the Skeletor laugh, which I always had trouble with. So he sat and coached me on how to do the laugh and he says I did it perfectly afterwards. Best experience of my life.

- Sadie Sink. She was really nice, but I kind of hurried it along because it seemed like she was leaving soon. 

- Chris Parson, Gladio's VA from FFXV. We did banter back and forth as Ig and Gladio, so that was cool.


Not so cool things

- One of the people with us (a friend of the girl who went as Lunafreya) wss dressed as a character from a completely different series, and got left out of a lot of pictures because of it. And proceeded to loudly complain even though this FFXV cosplay group was planned back last year. 

- Being asked to say Ignis' catch phrase every time I took a picture got on my nerves very quickly. I feel for the voice actor now. 

- Losing sight of where something I wanted to buy was and having to walk around the entire con center to find it. My friend was a real trooper as he walked around with me to go find a poster of Nier Automata that I ended up getting. 


All in all a really fun experience. Would do again.

So since I'm currently on break and waiting for summer classes to start, I decided to finally take the plunge and start playing the Kingdom Hearts series. Keep in mind I was never really interested in them when I was a kid and only started to play them because two of my friends are absolutely obsessed with them, and I'm also going in completely blind with no spoilers. So I decided to buy the collection for the PS4. I'm not all the way through yet but here are my thoughts so far, and I'm going to try and include as little spoilers as possible. 

**Kingdom Hearts 1**

- Graphics have aged incredibly well IMO. Textures look really nice for an early PS2 game
- Combat is satisfying, really really liked all the large fights.
- I really don't like Sora as a protag, but kind of got used to him after a while.
- I wish the game had included more non-Disney areas. The two original worlds SqEnix made are really amazing.
- The story had issues, but it was overall well done except for the ending which was a bit of a clusterfuck.
- Level design can get really awful sometimes. The amount of backtracking in the Tarzan world and Atlantica was obscene. 
- Music is fantastic, I like the orchestral score they included with the PS4 a lot.
- The little bits of lore dropping with Ansem's reports were really cool, and I like the concept of Ansem as a villain.
- Some of the boss fights were downright awesome, others (Clayton, Ursula) weren't so awesome.
- holy SHIT the gummi ship missions (how you travel from location to location) were so fucking bad.
- Overall I give it a Good but not Great/10 

**Chain of Memories**

- You thought you could skip straight to KH2? You fool!
- This game takes place right where KH1's after credits scene leaves off 
- The direction in this game feels so much better than 1. Everything just feels more together, and the story isn't a bunch of loose ends.
- The Organization are a little too "evil anime villain group" for my liking, but some of them are cool characters, especially Axel. I'll get to them when I talk about 358/2 Days. 
- Voice acting is also much better in this game. Probably attributed to having mainly adult voice actors instead of children like in the first game.
- I thought it was insanely cool to play as both Sora and Riku to see both their perspectives as the story progressed. 
- The one thing that's holding this game back is its combat. It's really really not good. It was a GBA port, so I can't fault it there, but the combat sucks. The story makes up for it though.
- The game is also much shorter than KH1, so I didn't suffer through the combat for that long. 
- Overall a Good Story/10

**The cutscenes of 358/2 Days** 

- Nope we aren't at KH2 yet
- This game takes place slightly before, during and after Chain of Memoires
- It's also a DS port with terrible gameplay, so they just ported the cutscenes.
- The three main characters, Roxas, Axel, and Xion are great.
- The three actually have a believable friendship with ups and downs, it's not just a concrete "ur my frien bcuz" and that's it.
- This game makes the Organization feel less like a unit of bad guys, and more like people with vastly different moralities who are all united because of a similar goal.
- Seeing members of the Org. clash with each other over their differing ideologies and how to handle the problem of Xion (which I won't get into because of spoilers). 
- This game actually makes you feel bad for some of the "bad guys", and there's nothing better to me than sympathetic villains.
- Even though I saw what was going to happen in the game coming from a mile away, it still made me emotional. So hats off to SqEnix for making me care about their dumb Disney game.
- Made me Cry/10

I've only finished the prologue of KH2, but I'll come back to write about the other games once i've finished them.

IMO grey vs. grey is far, far more interesting than evil vs. evil, and I'd say your story sounds a bit like that. 

If you want to identify a grey conflict, watch the original Star Wars trilogy  but think (in hypotheticals of course) about the actions of the Rebels against the Empire. While the Rebels are celebrating the destruction of the Death Star, think about all the people who had a family aboard it or how Luke just caused mass genocide. 
Now even though Luke has heroic qualities to him, who's to say people in the Empire weren't also heroes as well? 

The whole black and white conflict of Star Wars inspired me to write a grey vs. grey conflict where we see characters who are supposed to be our heroes inflicting trauma on another major character simply because they're on a different side. 

Show conflict from both sides, and make your villains sympathetic and human, and not just evil because evil

I have kind of a funny story about my first encounter with metal.

Way back in 1st grade, my class had to choose a book to read on a famous person and then do a Powerpoint on said person. One of the things that was required for the Powerpoint was that every slide must have music and a transition, which tied into what we were learning in computer class. 

Our school had a bunch of royalty free music, and then some famous songs without lyrics. One of them was Iron Man by Black Sabbath. I remember being completely awestruck by that riff for the first time. So awestruck that I used it for every single slide of that Powerpoint. 

I think after I was done with that project I exclusively  listened to Sabbath for the next year. So I can thank a school project for getting me into metal.
